chapter_title: Care and Maintenance of Fabrics in Institutions

concepts.title: Two Aspects of Fabric Care
concepts.definition: Caring for fabrics means guarding the material against physical harm and mending whatever harm use has caused, while also refreshing how it looks -- lifting stains and dirt so the texture and visual character survive to the end of the material's expected service life.
concepts.formula: care = damage prevention and repair plus appearance renewal
concepts.key_idea: Laundering is both science and art: principles guide it, but skill delivers the pleasing finish.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe203.txt, Introduction and Basic Concepts (approx lines 20-49)

solution_steps.explain: structural protection and mending on one side, stain and dirt removal on the other
fibre content, yarn and construction, finishes and end use

worked_examples.q: Fabric care guards against harm and also renews what: appearance or ownership?

concepts.title: Washing Machines and Their Types
concepts.definition: Machines load from the top or the front; by control they run fully automatic on a single setting, semi automatic with operator intervention each cycle in two tub form, or manually operated where half or more of the work stays with the person.
concepts.formula: machine classes -- top or front loading, crossed with automatic, semi automatic, manual
concepts.key_idea: A fully automatic unit handles filling, temperature, wash and rinses without help; semi automatic machines need filling and draining by hand every cycle.
question_patterns: differentiate between top loading and front loading machines
distinguish fully automatic, semi automatic and manually operated machines
which machine type needs the operator at every rinse cycle
what defines a manually operated washing machine

solution_steps.explain: top versus front access
one setting machines, two tub helped machines, hand powered machines

worked_examples.q: Which machines load through a door at the front: front loaders or top loaders?

concepts.title: Wash Motions and Water Extraction
concepts.definition: Every machine works by keeping fabric moving in the wash liquor -- agitator blades churn a current in top loaders, a vertical pulsator vibrates water through them, and front loaders tumble clothes through water in a revolving perforated cylinder; afterwards water leaves by spin alone, by bottom drain then spin, or by the best route, draining during the spin.
concepts.formula: motions -- agitation plus pulsation plus tumbling; extraction -- spin plus drain plus combined
concepts.key_idea: Spin speed sets how much water leaves the load, from 333 up to 1100 rpm, but near dry spinning invites stubborn wrinkles; about 600 to 620 rpm is optimal.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe203.txt, washing, rinsing, extraction and speed (approx lines 116-181)
question_patterns: name the three washing actions used in machines

list the three ways of extracting water after a wash

solution_steps.action: pair each motion with its machine
solution_steps.explain: agitation and pulsation ride in top loaders, tumbling in front loaders
combined bottom drain with spin extracts best because it clears settled and suspended dirt together

worked_examples.q: Front loaders clean by which motion: tumbling or agitation?

concepts.title: Driers and Their Air Circulation
concepts.definition: Tumbler driers move air two ways: a fast stream of low temperature room air heated as it passes through the load and exhausted out, or a slow moving high temperature stream whose moist exhaust leaves the drum humid.
concepts.formula: circulation choice -- fast cool air or slow hot air
concepts.key_idea: The low temperature high velocity route keeps room temperature and humidity normal; the hot slow route exhausts very humid air.
question_patterns: compare the two circulation systems used in driers
why does the slow hot drier exhaust very humid air
which drier system keeps the room atmosphere normal
where does room air enter and leave a drier

solution_steps.explain: low temperature, high velocity, exhausts dry
high temperature, slow fan driven flow, exhausts moist

worked_examples.q: Which circulation exhausts very humid air: slow hot air or fast cool air?

concepts.title: Ironing and Hot Pressing
concepts.definition: Ironing smooths the wrinkles that use and washing leave, while pressing sets creases into sleeves, trouser legs and pleats; thermostats match metal sole heat to the fabric, steam eases the work, and irons span roughly 1.5 to 3.5 kg with charcoal models still seen in India.
concepts.formula: finish work -- smoothing wrinkles plus setting creases
concepts.key_idea: Heavy household articles like curtains call for heavier irons, while light ones suit daily apparel.
question_patterns: differentiate between ironing and pressing
how does a thermostat protect fabrics during ironing
what is a charcoal iron
what weight range do electric irons cover and which articles need heavier ones
which garments need creases set by pressing

solution_steps.explain: removing wrinkles versus imposing creases
heated sole, thermostat, steam system, weight choices

worked_examples.q: Setting creases into sleeves and pleats is called what: pressing or folding?

concepts.title: Laundry Services: Dhobi to Commercial Laundry
concepts.definition: Household washing handles daily clothes; professional workers collect from homes and hostels and wash at marked town ghats; commercial laundries and dry cleaners take bigger articles, organised into sections for washing, extraction, drying, pressing, dry cleaning, fibre specific work, dyeing and finishes, with invoices and code tags tracking every item.
concepts.formula: service ladder -- household plus professional worker plus commercial laundry plus dry cleaner
concepts.key_idea: Commercial machines take 100 kg or more per cycle against 5 to 10 kg at home, and code tags tie each article to its invoice.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe203.txt, service levels and commercial sections (approx lines 221-284)

solution_steps.explain: home washing, hired workers, shops with transport, dry cleaning
damage noted at intake, invoice per customer, matching tags on items

worked_examples.q: Commercial machines take how many kilograms or more per cycle: 100 or 1?

concepts.title: Hospital Laundry and Its Process
concepts.definition: A hospital laundry puts hygiene, cleanliness and disinfection first: soiled linen is collected from wards and theatres, sorted, washed in hundred kilogram machines, hydro extracted, dried, pressed, mended or condemned, packed and distributed, with infection prone items replaced by burnable disposables.
concepts.formula: process chain -- collection plus transport plus sorting plus wash plus extraction plus dry plus press plus mend plus pack plus distribute
concepts.key_idea: Hospital cottons carry dyes of excellent wash fastness; starching and whitening rank below cleanliness, and only blankets are woollen.
concepts.textbook_ref: lehe203.txt, hospital laundry and process steps (approx lines 296-344)
question_patterns: list the steps of laundry functioning in a hospital

solution_steps.explain: from ward collection through sorting, washing, extraction, drying, finishing to distribution

worked_examples.q: Which laundry puts hygiene and disinfection first: hospital or hotel?

concepts.title: Hotel Laundry Priorities
concepts.definition: Hospitality laundries chase looks: mixed fibre articles must emerge starched, perfectly pressed and correctly folded, guests' personal laundry gets handled on request, and smaller hotels link up with outside commercial laundries instead of running their own plant.
concepts.formula: hotel priority -- aesthetics plus final finish plus guest service
concepts.key_idea: Hospitals wash for hygiene, hotels finish for beauty -- the same machines, opposite emphases.
question_patterns: how does a hotel laundry differ from a hospital laundry in emphasis
which finishing treatments matter most in the hospitality sector

solution_steps.explain: disinfection versus aesthetics
starching, ironing, pressing, perfect folding, guest items

worked_examples.q: Which laundry chases starched, pressed and folded looks: hotel or hospital?

concepts.title: Careers in Laundry and Fabric Care
concepts.section: Preparing for a Career and Scope
concepts.definition: The field demands command of the material's fibre, yarn, construction and finishes, of the cleaning processes and chemicals, and of the machinery; short laundry management courses offer training, placement and startup help, and specialisation in textile science opens jobs in airlines, shipping, railways, hotels and hi-tech hospitals or one's own service venture.
concepts.formula: knowledge triad -- material plus processes and chemicals plus machinery
concepts.key_idea: Working women in metros and the nursing home boom make fabric care a promising entrepreneurial field.
question_patterns: which knowledge areas must a laundry professional master
what do laundry management short term courses offer
which employers hire fabric care specialists
why is practical internship needed in this trade
what entrepreneurial openings exist in fabric care services

solution_steps.explain: fibre and finish effects, processes, reagents, machines
short courses with stipend training, textile science specialisations, self employment

worked_examples.q: Laundry careers demand command of material, processes and which third area: machinery or poetry?

concepts.title: Stain Removal Practice
concepts.definition: A stain is foreign matter absorbed into fabric that needs targeted treatment before washing; the right treatment depends on identifying the stain, its age, and the fibre -- cold water and salt for blood, methylated spirit for ball pen and lipstick, boiling water through tea marks, sour milk or oxalic acid for ink -- always against an untreated control sample.
concepts.formula: treatment choice -- stain identity plus age plus fibre type
concepts.key_idea: Fresh blood washes out in cold water and dilute ammonia, but hot water sets it; old stains call for salt steeping or stronger reagents by fibre.

solution_steps.explain: the table branches on all three

worked_examples.q: Fresh blood washes out in cold water but which kind of water sets it: hot or cold?

concepts.title: Linen Stock Requirement
concepts.definition: A hospital plans linen by multiplying beds by the minimum sets held per bed, then pieces per set -- sheet, draw sheet and pillow slip -- so the store always covers every bed even at peak washing turnover.
concepts.key_idea: Six sets per bed with three pieces each means an eighteen piece stock for every bed on the rolls.
question_patterns: a 500 bed hospital keeps a minimum of 6 linen sets per bed with 3 pieces per set; how many pieces must the store hold

solution_steps.explain: multiply the bed count by the sets held per bed
multiply the sets by the pieces in each set

worked_examples.q: Six sets per bed with three pieces each means how many pieces per bed: eighteen or six?

concepts.title: Daily Sheet Changes in Special Wards
concepts.definition: Operation theatre, maternity and labour room sheets can be changed five or more times a day, so the daily wash burden for such a zone is the zone's bed count multiplied by the changes each bed needs per day.
concepts.key_idea: At five changes, even a small forty bed zone pushes two hundred sheets into the daily cycle.
question_patterns: a maternity ward of 40 beds needs 5 sheet changes per bed daily; how many sheets enter the wash each day

work out the daily linen turnover for a high change zone

solution_steps.explain: each change puts one sheet into the cycle

worked_examples.q: At five changes a day, a forty-bed zone pushes how many sheets into daily wash: 200 or 45?

concepts.title: Hydro-Extractor Moisture Arithmetic
concepts.definition: A hydro extractor spins off sixty to seventy per cent of the moisture, so whatever remains for the drier is one hundred minus the percentage removed.
concepts.key_idea: At a mid 65 per cent extraction, about 35 per cent of the moisture still awaits the drier.
question_patterns: a hydro extractor removes 65 per cent of the moisture from a load; what per cent remains

find the residual moisture percentage when the extractor's removal rate is stated
a load enters the drier with 60 per cent moisture already removed; how much remains
compute the share of moisture the drier must handle after hydro extraction

solution_steps.action: subtract the removed share from one hundred
solution_steps.explain: the remainder is the moisture still held by the fabric

worked_examples.q: A hydro-extractor spins off sixty to seventy percent of the what: moisture or colour?

concepts.title: Machine Capacity Ratio
concepts.definition: Commercial washers handle 100 kilogram or more per cycle while domestic machines manage 5 to 10 kilograms, so the industrial advantage is the commercial capacity divided by the domestic one.
concepts.key_idea: Against a 5 kilogram home machine, a 100 kilogram plant machine washes twenty times the load each cycle.
question_patterns: a plant machine washes 100 kg per cycle against a domestic 5 kg machine; how many times greater is its capacity
compute the capacity ratio between an institutional washer and a home washer
a 100 kg commercial unit is compared with a 10 kg domestic one; find the ratio
how many domestic loads equal one commercial cycle when both capacities are stated
calculate how many times more linen a commercial machine handles per cycle

solution_steps.explain: commercial capacity over domestic capacity gives the multiplier

worked_examples.q: Against a 5 kg home machine, a 100 kg plant machine washes how many times the load: twenty or two?
